page: Microsoft Azure M64bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz, offering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading. It includes 512 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on remote premium block storage for persistence.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong memory throughput alongside robust parallel processing capacity. Memory bandwidth benchmarks recorded 216.83 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations and 92.52 GB/sec in large-block write operations. The dedicated compute architecture produced strong results in database operations and key-value throughput, reaching 71.51 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Compute testing shows high throughput in Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression, while raw multi-core stress testing registers within the median range. The absence of local disk requires remote block storage integration, making disk I/O subject to network performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M64bs_v3 targets enterprise environments requiring large memory capacities and dedicated compute resources without the cost of high-density attached local flash storage. Its memory-to-core ratio and AMX support make it well suited for large in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise ERP deployments, heavy static web serving, and CPU-driven large language model inference.
description: Microsoft Azure M64bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processor clocked at 4.0 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, accompanied by 512 GB of RAM, equating to 8 GB of memory per core. The processor features 105 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration instructions. The server does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external premium block storage. Benchmark assessments highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 216 GB/sec and Redis SET throughput exceeding 71 million operations per second, along with capable multi-threaded decompression and software compilation metrics. With high memory density balanced against dedicated compute, this instance is suited for in-memory caching systems, large relational databases, enterprise transactional engines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
